claims.explanation: Amisulpride is a high-affinity D2/D3 dopamine receptor antagonist, so selective killing most likely occurs in cancer lines that express DRD2/DRD3 and depend on dopamine receptor signaling for proliferation. PI3K/AKT pathway activation (e.g., PIK3CA, PTEN, EGFR mutations) may further sensitize by cooperating with dopamine receptor signaling, while chromatin-remodeling mutations (e.g., KMT2D) and ATM loss may protect by reducing drug-induced growth inhibition.
